audits.title: An audit of primary surgical treatment for women with ovarian cancer referred to a cancer centre.
audits.standard: National and international guidelines for initial surgery and staging of ovarian cancer
audits.setting: Christie Cancer Centre, Manchester, and referring hospitals

cycle1.result: 92% presented via outpatient clinic (elective surgery); up to seven consultants per hospital operated; less than half underwent the recommended surgical procedure

audits.other_findings: Surgery was spread across many consultants, each treating few patients.
audits.citation: Sengupta PS, Jayson GC, Slade RJ, Eardley A, Radford JA. An audit of primary surgical treatment for women with ovarian cancer referred to a cancer centre. Br J Cancer. 1999;80(3-4):444-447. doi:10.1038/sj.bjc.6690376. PMID: 10408851.

audits.title: Clinical governance network for clinical audit to improve quality in epithelial ovarian cancer management.
audits.standard: Evidence-based quality indicators for ovarian cancer workup and treatment

cycle1.result: Histological diagnosis in 222 (76.3%); FIGO surgical staging reported in 206 (70.9%); residual disease not always reported.

audits.intervention: Identification of reference centres and promotion of centralisation; new region-wide audit planned.
audits.other_findings: Only 2 high-volume hospitals; no standard number of neoadjuvant chemotherapy cycles.
audits.citation: Mandato VD, Abrate M, De Iaco P, Pirillo D, Ciarlini G, Leoni M, et al.. Clinical governance network for clinical audit to improve quality in epithelial ovarian cancer management. J Ovarian Res. 2013;6(1):19. doi:10.1186/1757-2215-6-19. PMID: 23547941.

audits.title: Is Ovarian Cancer Being Managed According to Clinical Guidelines? Evidence From a Population-Based Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines for ovarian cancer surgery and chemotherapy

cycle1.result: 215 (62.5%) had care with curative intent; surgery adherent to guidelines in 35.2% and chemotherapy in 87.8%.

audits.other_findings: Guideline-adherent chemotherapy was linked to lower risk of death (HR 0.49); authors call for reorganising the pathway.
audits.citation: Sobrero S, Pagano E, Piovano E, Bono L, Ceccarelli M, Ferrero A, et al.. Is Ovarian Cancer Being Managed According to Clinical Guidelines? Evidence From a Population-Based Clinical Audit. Int J Gynecol Cancer. 2016;26(9):1615-1623. doi:10.1097/igc.0000000000000830. PMID: 27779546.

audits.title: Regional Audit and Feedback Intervention to Improve Quality of Care in Ovarian Cancer Treatment: The Easy-Net Experience.
audits.standard: Key recommendations and indicators from international guidelines (global adherence)
audits.setting: Gynaecological units treating ovarian cancer in the Piemonte Regional Cancer Care Network
audits.intervention: Audit and feedback with quarterly feedback meetings.

cycle2.result: Global adherence rose to 70.4% (2.1% increase every 6 months, 95% CI 1.6 to 2.6).

audits.other_findings: Treatment in high-volume centres and MDT discussion increased; a 10% increase in adherence was associated with improved 5-year survival (HR 0.91). Earlier regional audit in 2009.
audits.citation: Piovano E, Ferrero A, Ciccone G, Camanni M, Castiglione A, Ceccarelli M, et al.. Regional Audit and Feedback Intervention to Improve Quality of Care in Ovarian Cancer Treatment: The Easy-Net Experience. JCO Oncol Pract. 2026. doi:10.1200/op-25-00309. PMID: 41610384.

audits.title: Clinical auditing as an instrument to improve care for patients with ovarian cancer: The Dutch Gynecological Oncology Audit (DGOA).
audits.standard: Predefined DGOA quality indicators, including start of therapy within 28 days

cycle1.result: Start of therapy within 28 days fell from 68.7% in 2014 to 62.7% in 2018; case ascertainment 98.3% in 2016.

audits.other_findings: Hospitals varied on quality indicators; best practices were to be shared with participants.
audits.citation: Baldewpersad Tewarie NMS, van Driel WJ, van Ham M, Wouters MW, Kruitwagen R, participants of the Dutch Gynecological Oncology Collaborator Group. Clinical auditing as an instrument to improve care for patients with ovarian cancer: The Dutch Gynecological Oncology Audit (DGOA). Eur J Surg Oncol. 2021;47(7):1691-1697. doi:10.1016/j.ejso.2021.01.019. PMID: 33581966.
